question: Which file extension holds the compiled, runnable version of an Oracle form?
options: .fmx
.fmb
.fmt
.pll
explanation: The .fmb file is the editable source and compiling it produces the .fmx executable that the Forms runtime loads. Libraries follow the same pattern with .pll and .plx.

question: Which trigger fires when the user clicks a push button?
options: WHEN-BUTTON-PRESSED
WHEN-NEW-ITEM-INSTANCE
KEY-NEXT-ITEM
POST-CHANGE
explanation: WHEN-BUTTON-PRESSED is attached to the button item and runs on each click. WHEN-NEW-ITEM-INSTANCE fires when the cursor merely enters an item.

question: When does a POST-QUERY trigger fire?
options: After each record is fetched into the block, before it is displayed
Once, immediately before the query is sent to the database
Only after the last record of the query has been fetched
Whenever the user commits a change to a queried record
explanation: POST-QUERY runs per fetched record, which is why it is the usual place to populate non-database items such as a looked-up description.

question: Which built-in moves the input focus to a different block?
options: GO_BLOCK
GO_ITEM
NEXT_SET
SET_BLOCK_PROPERTY
explanation: GO_BLOCK navigates to the named block and puts the cursor in its first enterable item. GO_ITEM navigates within a block to a specific item.

question: What does :SYSTEM.MODE return while the form is waiting for query criteria?
options: ENTER-QUERY
QUERY
NORMAL
CRITERIA
explanation: :SYSTEM.MODE returns NORMAL, ENTER-QUERY, or QUERY. ENTER-QUERY means the user is typing criteria; QUERY means a query is currently executing.

question: What is a record group most commonly used for?
options: Supplying the rows displayed by a list of values
Grouping items so they can be disabled together
Defining the physical layout of a block
Storing the form's commit-time validation rules
explanation: A record group is an in-memory result set, and an LOV is attached to one to get its rows. Record groups can be static or built from a query.

question: What does the COMMIT_FORM built-in do?
options: Validates the form, writes pending changes to the database, and commits the transaction
Writes pending changes but leaves the transaction open
Discards pending changes and requeries the block
Commits only the current record, ignoring other blocks
explanation: COMMIT_FORM performs validation, posts the changes, and then issues the database commit, ending the transaction.

question: How does POST differ from COMMIT_FORM?
options: POST writes changes to the database but keeps the transaction open, so they can still be rolled back
POST commits immediately, while COMMIT_FORM only validates
POST affects only the current block, while COMMIT_FORM affects the current record
There is no difference; POST is an alias for COMMIT_FORM
explanation: POST makes changes visible to later SQL in the same transaction without committing, which is useful when a called form must see the parent's uncommitted rows.

question: Which trigger is the right place to validate the value a user typed into a single item?
options: WHEN-VALIDATE-ITEM
WHEN-NEW-RECORD-INSTANCE
PRE-FORM
ON-ERROR
explanation: WHEN-VALIDATE-ITEM fires when the item's value has changed and validation is due, and raising FORM_TRIGGER_FAILURE there keeps the cursor on the bad item.

question: What is the relationship between a window and a canvas?
options: A canvas is the surface that items are painted on, and it is displayed inside a window
A window is painted onto a canvas, which acts as the outer frame
They are two names for the same object in the layout editor
A canvas can only hold non-database items; a window holds the rest
explanation: Items live on canvases, and each canvas is assigned to a window that provides the frame, title bar, and scrollbars. One window can show several canvases.

question: When does the PRE-FORM trigger fire?
options: Once, after the form is loaded but before it is displayed
Every time a new record is created
Once, immediately after the user exits the form
Before each query is executed
explanation: PRE-FORM is the usual home for one-off initialisation such as setting globals or hiding items, because nothing has been drawn yet.

question: What does the EXECUTE_QUERY built-in do?
options: Opens the query criteria screen without fetching anything
Flushes the current block and runs its query, fetching records from the database
Runs the last SQL statement the user typed
Validates the block without touching the database
explanation: EXECUTE_QUERY clears the block's existing records and populates it from the database, which is why unsaved changes prompt the user first.

question: What does a master-detail relation between two blocks provide?
options: A shared canvas for both blocks
A guarantee that each block commits in its own transaction
Automatic coordination, so the detail block requeries when the master record changes
Identical item properties across both blocks
explanation: Forms generates the relation triggers and procedures that keep the detail block in step with the current master record, including the deletion rule you choose.

question: How does a display item differ from a text item?
options: A display item cannot be navigated to or edited by the user
A display item can only hold numeric values
A display item must be based on a database column
A display item is invisible at runtime
explanation: Display items are read-only and take no part in navigation, which makes them the right choice for looked-up descriptions and computed totals.

question: How does MESSAGE differ from showing an alert?
options: MESSAGE shows a modal dialog; an alert writes to the status line
MESSAGE writes to the status line and carries on; an alert is modal and waits for a response
Both are modal, but MESSAGE cannot include variable text
MESSAGE only works while the form is in ENTER-QUERY mode
explanation: Use MESSAGE for information the user does not have to acknowledge, and an alert when you need a decision or want to be certain the message was seen.

question: What changes when you write an ON-INSERT trigger?
options: It runs after Forms has already inserted the row
It adds validation without altering how the insert happens
It replaces the default insert processing for that block entirely
It fires only when the insert fails
explanation: ON- triggers override default DML, so your code becomes responsible for performing the insert, typically via a stored procedure or INSERT_RECORD.

question: Which values can :SYSTEM.FORM_STATUS return?
options: VALID or INVALID
NORMAL, ENTER-QUERY, or QUERY
TRUE or FALSE
CHANGED, QUERY, or NEW
explanation: CHANGED means there are unsaved changes, QUERY means every record matches what was queried, and NEW means no record has been created or fetched yet.

question: What does NEXT_RECORD do when the cursor is already on the last fetched record?
options: Raises an error
Creates a new empty record, if the block allows insertion
Wraps around to the first record
Requeries the block
explanation: Moving past the last record creates a new one in an insertable block, which is how users add rows by simply navigating downwards.

question: Which file extension holds a PL/SQL library's editable source?
options: .pll
.plx
.fmb
.mmb
explanation: A .pll compiles to a .plx, mirroring the .fmb to .fmx pair for forms and .mmb to .mmx for menus.

question: When does WHEN-VALIDATE-RECORD fire?
options: Before any item in the record has been entered
Only at commit time
After the record's items are validated, when record-level validation is due
Each time the user types a character
explanation: Because it runs once the whole record is populated, it is the right place for rules spanning several items, such as checking an end date falls after a start date.

question: How does CALL_FORM differ from OPEN_FORM?
options: CALL_FORM closes the calling form before opening the new one
CALL_FORM keeps the calling form in memory and suspends it until the called form exits
OPEN_FORM can only open forms held in the same directory
They behave identically; CALL_FORM is simply the older name
explanation: CALL_FORM is modal with respect to its caller, while OPEN_FORM runs the new form independently in the same session. NEW_FORM replaces the caller altogether.

question: What does an LOV's "Automatic Select" property do?
options: Picks the first row of the LOV without displaying it
Refreshes the underlying record group each time the LOV opens
Validates the typed value against the database on every keystroke
Returns the value and dismisses the LOV automatically when only one row matches
explanation: It saves the user a keystroke in the common case where their partial entry narrows the list to exactly one row.

question: What makes a block a control block?
options: It is not based on a database table or view
It contains only push buttons
It is always shown in its own window
It can never hold more than one record
explanation: With no base table, a control block never queries or commits. It suits toolbars, search criteria, and calculated summary items.

question: What is a KEY- trigger for?
options: Recording which key the user pressed, for auditing
Redefining what a particular function key does in the form
Enforcing the block's primary key
Encrypting keystrokes before they reach the database
explanation: A KEY- trigger such as KEY-NEXT-ITEM replaces that key's built-in behaviour, so if you still want the original action you must call the matching built-in yourself.

question: What is SET_ITEM_PROPERTY used for?
options: Permanently changing the item's definition in the .fmb
Copying properties from one item to another at design time
Setting the item's value
Changing an item's properties at runtime, such as enabling or hiding it
explanation: It affects the current session only. To change a value rather than a property, assign to :block.item or use COPY.
